text: You're in a busy crowd, trying to get somewhere. You move, then stop, then move again. It feels chaotic, frustrating. You just want to get through.
You try to push harder, zig-zagging through gaps. But every time you speed up, you just get stuck even tighter. Why does this always happen?
You blame the slow people ahead, or the distracted ones. Surely, if everyone just *moved*, we'd all get through. It feels like simple bad etiquette.
But the problem isn't individuals; it's the system. A tiny hesitation by one person creates a gap. Others rush to fill it, increasing local density.
This extra density forces those ahead to slow, creating another gap. A ripple effect starts, a chain reaction of stops and starts.
It's a "jam wave" propagating backwards, even if no one is truly standing still. Now you see the invisible system: crowds always create their own delays.
